name: remake
desc: GNU Make with improved error handling, tracing, and a debugger
why: A debugger for GNU Make that traces build execution is a lovely way to watch a program run, though niche.

brief.what_it_is: remake is a patched build of GNU Make that adds better error reporting, tracing, target listing, graph visualization, profiling, and a debugger. The latest version is based on GNU Make 4.3 source, with branches for 4.2, 4.1, 3.82, and 3.81. It takes a Makefile and runs the build as usual, but prints more about what it is doing and why. Its output is text on the terminal, and profile output that can be opened in KCachegrind. The homepage also mentions debuggers for Python 3, Python 2, GNU Bash, Z Shell, Korn shell, Perl, and Node.js.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes remake as an enhanced GNU Make that adds improved error reporting, better tracing, profiling and a debugger. The homepage's own tagline is "GNU Make with comprehensible tracing and a debugger."
brief.how_it_works: The README says the project is patched GNU Make 4.3 sources with the added features. Tracing, target listing, and show-parent are switched on with command-line options, and the debugger is documented on the Read the Docs site. The README does not explain the internals in detail.

commands_seen.context: Option named in the README as the 'Example showing --tasks feature' (animated GIF). Lists targets. Shown as a flag only; the README gives no full command line.
Option named in the README for tracing build execution, with -x as its short form. Shown as a flag only; the README gives no full command line.
Option named in the README that shows the parent of a target, with -c as its short form. Shown as a flag only; the README gives no full command line.
Option named in the README that produces profiling output, which the README says can be displayed with KCachegrind. Shown as a flag only; the README gives no full command line.

brief.install_notes: The homepage links a SourceForge download (version 4.3+dbg-1.5 in the GitHub README's link), a GitHub page, and a Doxygen source-code reference. The README points to Read the Docs for installation instructions, which I did not fetch. Nothing else about accounts, runtimes, or first-run configuration appeared in what I read. Homebrew is the install route here.
brief.standout: It is a debugger for Make itself, which is unusual, and the README shows a trace view and a profile view through KCachegrind. The same debugging idea is applied to several other scripting languages, per the homepage.
brief.status: unknown. The GitHub README has a Travis CI badge pointing at the remake-4-3 branch and a Repology packaging badge, and the SourceForge download is versioned 4.3+dbg-1.5. I found no release date or last-commit date in what I read, so I cannot say whether it is current.
brief.caveats: The homepage text has typos ("enahanced", "some cool debuggers"), so treat it as informal. The README gives no commands in code blocks, only option names in captions. The debugger coverage list is from the homepage only, and I did not verify it. The older branches cover GNU Make 4.2, 4.1, 3.82, and 3.81 and are separate builds. The Read the Docs install page was not checked, so build requirements are unknown.
quotes: remake is an enahanced version of GNU Make that adds improved error reporting, better tracing, profiling and a debugger.

The wiki also has information, including links to videos, and information for developers.
